# zillizcloud_cluster_restore (Resource)

Restores an existing backup into a new Dedicated cluster in the source cluster's region. Name, description, and CU size are updated in place. Changing the source, backup, target project, collection status, or version selection replaces the cluster and can delete data added after the restore. Tracking the restore job requires observability read permission on the target project. A failed or canceled job fails the apply and protects the recorded target from automatic deletion. If the target disappears, a subsequent plan can retry the restore. An observation timeout records the target and job with a warning so refresh can resume tracking. Until success has been observed, a job-read failure blocks refresh and apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "zillizcloud_cluster_restore" "from_backup" {
  source_cluster_id = "in01-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
  backup_id         = "backup-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
  project_id        = "proj-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
  cluster_name      = "restored-cluster"
  cu_size           = 1

  # Choose a version returned by the restore candidates query for this backup.
  version = {
    milvus_version = "2.6.x"
    channel        = "ORIGIN"
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "60m"
  }
}

output "restore_status" {
  value = zillizcloud_cluster_restore.from_backup.restore_status
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `backup_id` (String) ID of the backup to restore.
- `cluster_name` (String) Name of the restored cluster.
- `cu_size` (Number) Number of compute units for the restored cluster.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the target project.
- `source_cluster_id` (String) ID of the cluster that owns the backup.

### Optional

- `collection_status` (String) Whether to KEEP or RELEASE the restored collections. Defaults to RELEASE.
- `description` (String) Description of the restored cluster. When omitted, track the current description.
- `restore_version_policy` (String) Restore using the LATEST or ORIGINAL policy. Conflicts with version. Omit both to use the API default.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `version` (Attributes) Explicit version selected from the candidates for this backup. Conflicts with restore_version_policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--version))

### Read-Only

- `connect_address` (String) Endpoint of the restored cluster.
- `id` (String) ID of the new cluster.
- `job_id` (String) ID of the asynchronous restore job.
- `milvus_version` (String) Milvus version series currently reported by the restored cluster.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Default database password returned when the restore is submitted.
- `region_id` (String) Region of the restored cluster.
- `restore_status` (String) Latest known restore job status. If waiting times out, Terraform records the accepted cluster and job so refresh can continue tracking them.
- `username` (String) Default database username returned when the restore is submitted.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Time to wait for the restore to finish. Defaults to 45 minutes. After submission, a timeout produces a warning and keeps the cluster and job IDs in state.
- `delete` (String) Time allowed for the delete request. Defaults to 2 minutes.
- `update` (String) Time to apply cluster changes. Defaults to 30 minutes.


<a id="nestedatt--version"></a>
### Nested Schema for `version`

Required:

- `channel` (String) The channel of the selected Milvus version.
- `milvus_version` (String) Milvus version series, such as `2.6.x`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import an existing restored cluster without starting a new restore.
# Use target_cluster_id,source_cluster_id,backup_id for a configuration using restore defaults.
terraform import zillizcloud_cluster_restore.from_backup 'in01-target,in01-source,backup-abcdefghijklmnop'

# Append job_id,collection_status,version_or_policy when the configuration uses those settings.
# Leave an optional position empty to skip it. The collection status defaults to RELEASE.
# version_or_policy accepts a series and channel separated by a colon, or ORIGINAL or LATEST.
# Use the values from the original restore and verify that the next plan has no replacement.
terraform import zillizcloud_cluster_restore.from_backup 'in01-target,in01-source,backup-abcdefghijklmnop,job-abcdefghijklmnop,RELEASE,2.6.x:ORIGIN'

# Import reads the existing cluster. The credentials from the original restore are unavailable.
# If a restore failed and the target still exists, inspect it before deleting it outside Terraform.
# A later apply can retry after the failed target has been removed.
```
